title: POC scoping - workload modeling for Mercantile Bank
summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling. Goals: agree success criteria (latency SLOs, quality thresholds, cost targets), define QPS/concurrency targets, token distributions, and POC timeline (4 weeks). Action items: Redwood to run baseline benchmarks, customer to share sample dataset and firewall/VPC details, schedule baseline test next week.
next_steps: Redwood to run initial benchmark against a 10k-sample prompt set and share results (by 2027-06-09)
Customer to provide sample prompts + expected output distribution and S3 link (by 2027-06-04)
Schedule baseline load run with Mercantile infra team (tentative 2027-06-10)
Share Redwood security / SOC2 docs and NDA link
action_items: Ravi (Redwood SE): prepare benchmark harness and default config + provide test script
Lena (AE): send pricing sheet and pilot terms
Mark (Customer CTO): provide sample data access and IP allowlist info
Tom (Infra): confirm VPC peering options and outbound firewall rules
transcript: 00:00 Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a sec um 00:05 Mark Reynolds: yea thanks Lena 00:08 Lena Park: quick intro - I'm Lena, AE for Redwood Inference, joined by Ravi our SE and Marisol on solutions, can folks do quick intros? 00:18 Sarah Lee: Sarah, head of ML at Mercantile, running our chat assistant initiative 00:23 Tom Alvarez: Tom infra, i'll handle networking and security ask 00:27 Evelyn Ortiz: Evelyn, product, i'm owning success criteria 00:31 Ravi Singh: hi all, ravi from redwood, i'll be running the benchmarks and modelling the traffic 00:35 Mark Reynolds: cool 00:38 Lena Park: purpose today is to scope a POC - specifically workload characterization and traffic modeling: qps, concurrency, token dist, and agree on benchmarks and timeline 00:48 Sarah Lee: yep that's what we need, we're trying to replace our current hosted model infra, looking for better latency and cost predictability 00:55 Tom Alvarez: and we have some compliance constraints, must use VPC peering or dedicated, no open internet for inference 01:03 Lena Park: understood. quick qual: what are your current qps and peaks? 01:09 Mark Reynolds: our production chat volume is about 8 qps average, peaks around 60 qps during morning batch windows, concurrency typically around 20-30 active chats 01:20 Sarah Lee: token-wise input is short majority, ~40 tokens median but we have a long-tail where some requests hit 800-1k tokens, output avg is 80-150 but can sometimes stream for long sessions 01:33 Ravi Singh: okay that's helpful — so distribution: input median 40, 95th ~900, output avg 120 — any structured prompts or tool calls? 01:45 Sarah Lee: some tool calls, yes, and we do function-calling style structured outputs for payments flows 01:51 Lena Park: success criteria from your side, what would make POC successful? 01:56 Evelyn Ortiz: a few things: p95 latency under 400ms for async generation (we can tolerate a little more for very long tokens), quality on par with current model per our eval set (we'll share scoring), and per-token cost reduction of 20% min 02:10 Mark Reynolds: and we need private deployment option for regulated accounts — so proof that redwood private or dedicated fits our compliance 02:19 Ravi Singh: noted. For latency do you mean end-to-end or model only? 02:22 Tom Alvarez: end-to-end from our app through the inference endpoint, including networking 02:27 Ravi Singh: good — we'll include network hop sim in benchmarks. on model choice, do you have a head model or open model preference? 02:34 Sarah Lee: we'd like an open model variant initially, maybe a 13B quantized model as our baseline, but we want to compare a 70B for quality checks 02:42 Lena Park: makes sense; for the POC we'll run both: 13B quant quant and a 70B float/quant hybrid to show tradeoffs 02:49 Ravi Singh: can you share sample prompt set and the eval rubric? will need that to compute quality and latency per prompt class 02:55 Sarah Lee: yes sending after call, about 10k prompts sampled from prod 03:01 Lena Park: perfect. now on qps modelling - based on what you said, target steady-state for the POC should be 10 qps with burst tests to 75-100 qps to cover peak headroom 03:14 Ravi Singh: concur. we'll run steady-state 10 qps for 30 minutes to measure cost and p95, then 5-min bursts at 75 and 100 qps to measure saturation and tail latency 03:23 Tom Alvarez: for concurrency we need to see how session affinity and KV cache behave — do you simulate large numbers of concurrent sessions with cached prefixes? 03:31 Ravi Singh: yes we'll include prefix/KV cache scenarios: cold-path (no cache), warm path (cache hit rate ~60%), and hot-path (cache hit ~90%) to show effective token cost reductions 03:43 Lena Park: about tokens: we need distribution bins for benchmarking - 0-64, 65-256, 257-512, 513-1024 — sounds right? 03:53 Sarah Lee: yes that maps to our usage 03:56 Ravi Singh: great, we'll report p50/p95/p99 latency broken out by token bin and cost per 1k tokens as well 04:05 Mark Reynolds: what hardware will you run on for the dedicated runs? 04:09 Ravi Singh: we'll run on a mix — a8x or A100 equivalent for the 70B and 13B on T4/RTX-class with quantization; we'll note exact GPU SKUs in the report, and provide kernel-level perf notes (sometimes transcript: kernal vs kernel) 04:22 Tom Alvarez: note that our infra team prefers Vulcan cloud A-region, can you deploy a private POC there? 04:27 Lena Park: Redwood Private supports VPC in that region, we'll check capacity; if needed we can do a hosted bench and then a dedicated/private deploy for final run 04:36 Sarah Lee: security question: do you support customer-managed KMS and audit logging? 04:41 Marisol Chen: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations on private and dedicated, and we can push audit logs to your SIEM, we'll share docs 04:49 Mark Reynolds: and SOC2? 04:51 Lena Park: Redwood is SOC2 compliant — we'll attach the report, and also our data retention and RBAC docs 04:58 Ravi Singh: small note on measurement methodology: we'll run cold-start tests every hour during the run, and measure KV cache warm-up time — cold path will be simulated by rebooting worker nodes between runs 05:09 Sarah Lee: that might blow up our infra, can you sandbox the test in redwood-hosted environment but with realistic network latency added? 05:16 Ravi Singh: yes we can simulate network using WAN emulator and add your expected RTT, and also run a private deploy test if you want final signoff 05:25 Evelyn Ortiz: timeline — how long for the POC and deliverables? 05:29 Lena Park: we propose 4 weeks: week 1 access + data ingestion + config, week 2 baseline benchmarks (steady-state + bursts), week 3 model tuning and follow-ups, week 4 final runs + report and exec review 05:41 Mark Reynolds: sounds good, can we compress to 3 weeks? we need a faster decision 05:45 Ravi Singh: we can compress if customer provides prompt set and network access in week 0 and we focus on essentials — propose a 3-week accelerated track but keep 4-week default 05:55 Lena Park: ok we'll include both timelines in the SOW 05:58 Tom Alvarez: firewall / networking details: we'll need public IPs to allow or a peering tunnel — i'll send security contacts and allowlist 06:05 Marisol Chen: action: we'll need a sample stoplight of prompts by bin to seed the harness, and the expected scoring metric (BLEU/ROUGE/custom) 06:15 Sarah Lee: our score is a hybrid automated + human rating, we'll provide the rubric 06:21 Ravi Singh: good. on instrumentation we'll capture token counts, per-request latency, end-to-end RTT, GPU utilization, and model tail latencies 06:31 Mark Reynolds: cost target reminder: 20% per-token cost reduction vs current hosted provider, otherwise we'll struggle with ROI 06:38 Lena Park: understood — we'll show cost modeling and options: batching, quant profiles, and dedicated pools to hit that target or explain tradeoffs 06:45 Ravi Singh: one more technical: for streaming and function calls do you have strict real-time constraints? 06:50 Sarah Lee: streaming needs to be under 200ms p95 for user-facing flows; function calls can be looser 06:56 Lena Park: noted. any regulatory/regional residency needs? 06:59 Mark Reynolds: EU data for several accounts, need residency in eu-central for those customers 07:04 Lena Park: okay we'll note region constraints and routing policies 07:09 Evelyn Ortiz: can you share an example SOW and pilot pricing? 07:12 Lena Park: yes Lena: i'll send pilot terms and pricing today, Ravi will share benchmark plan and script, Marisol security docs 07:18 Ravi Singh: we'll also provide a short demo of the harness once it's ready 07:22 Tom Alvarez: one more: do you support per-route quotas and per-team RBAC? 07:27 Marisol Chen: yes RBAC and per-route quotas are supported on the console, and we can pre-configure for POC 07:33 Sarah Lee: okay good 07:35 Mark Reynolds: thanks, this was helpful 07:37 Lena Park: recap — we have success criteria: p95 latency <400ms end-to-end (200ms p95 for streaming), quality parity on eval set, 20% cost reduction; benchmarks: steady-state 10 qps 30m, bursts to 75/100, token bins and cache scenarios; timeline: 3-4 weeks; next: customer share prompts + allowlist, redwood run initial bench and share results 07:58 Evelyn Ortiz: i'll expect a calendar invite for the baseline run 08:02 Lena Park: we'll send invites and all artifacts. thanks everyone! 08:06 Mark Reynolds: thanks 08:08 END OF RECORDING
